constraints.action: receive at least 5 cmH2O of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)
use lower tidal volume and plateau pressure to protect the 'baby lung'
use PEEP and lung recruitment maneuvers (RM) to reduce the amount of non-aerated lung
ventilate in the prone position
receive HFNO as compared to conventional oxygen therapy
limit Vt to 4–8 mL/kg PBW
maintain plateau airway pressure (Pplat) < 30 cmH2O
measure and adjust Vt using PBW
use low tidal volume ventilation strategies (i.e., 4–8 ml/kg PBW)
use prolonged high-pressure recruitment maneuvers (defined as airway pressure maintained ≥ 35 cmH2O for at least one minute)
use routine PEEP titration with a higher PEEP/FiO2 strategy versus a lower PEEP/FiO2 strategy
use routine PEEP titration guided principally by respiratory mechanics
use brief high-pressure recruitment maneuvers (defined as airway pressure maintained ≥ 35 cmH2O for less than one minute)
use routine use of brief RMs
use continuous infusions of NMBA to reduce mortality in patients with moderate-to-severe ARDS not due to COVID-19
use ECCO2R for the treatment of ARDS not due to COVID-19 to prevent mortality outside of randomized controlled trials
start prone position in patients with ARDS receiving invasive mechanical ventilation early after intubation
apply proning for prolonged sessions (16 consecutive hours or more)
treat with ECMO in an ECMO center which meets defined organizational standards
adhere to a management strategy similar to that used in the EOLIA trial
have appropriate experience and expertise
have appropriate monitoring (e.g. clinical signs of respiratory distress, breathing pattern—tidal volume (Vt) and respiratory rate—and inspiratory effort) to avert P-SILI
consider how well individual patients may tolerate NIV and the risk of adverse events
apply low tidal volume and adjust PEEP during a period of stabilization prior to proning
abort the maneuver immediately if cardiovascular instability ensues
have an ECMO team with capacity to transfer patients on ECMO (mobile ECMO)
close monitoring is required to avoid delaying intubation and to regularly assess and manage comfort and tolerance
